 Télétravail - États-Unis et Canada seulement | Temps plein
 Rémunération:
 150 000 $ US (pour les personnes candidates résidant aux États-Unis)
 150 000 $ CA (pour les personnes candidates résidant au Canada)
 Le directeur principal ou la directrice principale de la stratégie joue un rôle central dans la façon dont l'agence réfléchit, planifie et génère de l'impact pour ses clients. Ce rôle est responsable de définir l'orientation stratégique des comptes prioritaires et de veiller à ce que les équipes média, création, SEO, CRM, web et analytique soient alignées sur un objectif d'affaires commun.
 Ce rôle exige un esprit axé sur les insights et la capacité de traduire des défis d'affaires complexes en une orientation stratégique claire. Le directeur principal ou la directrice principale de la stratégie pilotera le diagnostic de croissance, définira les priorités stratégiques et créera les liens entre les disciplines pour que l'exécution soit toujours alignée sur une intention claire et des résultats mesurables.
 Dans notre agence, la stratégie n'est pas une gamme de services, c'est notre façon de travailler. Le directeur principal ou la directrice principale de la stratégie veille à ce que les insights, la planification et la prise de décision soient intégrés à chaque étape du cycle de vie de nos partenariats clients.
 À propos de Level
 Nous sommes une agence de marketing de performance propulsée par l’IA — bâtie pour la précision, conçue pour évoluer et guidée par une mentalité scientifique. Chez Level, nous combinons stratégie, médias, création et intelligence machine pour livrer des résultats qui comptent. Chaque fois. À grande échelle.
 Nous avons été nommés parmi les meilleurs lieux de travail de Pittsburgh et reconnus comme l’une des entreprises à la croissance la plus rapide du classement Inc. 500. Nos clients œuvrent notamment en B2B, en éducation, en santé, en services financiers, en commerce électronique et dans plusieurs autres secteurs.
 Votre rôle et votre impact
 Vos responsabilités: 
 Orientation stratégique des comptes prioritaires: Vous dirigerez l'orientation stratégique de mandats clients à fort impact, en veillant à ce que les activités marketing soient alignées sur des objectifs d'affaires clairs et des occasions de croissance. Vous piloterez la phase de découverte, rédigerez des briefs stratégiques et transformerez les défis d'affaires en plans structurés et concrets.
 Planification stratégique et feuilles de route: Vous contribuerez aux cycles de planification annuels et trimestriels en élaborant des feuilles de route de croissance liées à des résultats mesurables. Vous clarifierez les priorités, définirez les indicateurs de succès et veillerez à ce que les équipes partagent une compréhension commune de l'intention stratégique.
 Élaboration des briefs stratégiques: Vous serez responsable de l'élaboration des briefs stratégiques qui définissent les objectifs d'affaires, les priorités de croissance, les insights sur l'audience, le positionnement, l'approche par canal, la logique d'investissement et les cadres de mesure. Ces briefs serviront de fondation pour aligner les équipes multidisciplinaires avant le début de l'exécution.
 Insights sur l'audience, le marché et la catégorie: Vous dirigerez l'élaboration des insights sur l'audience, de l'analyse concurrentielle et de la veille de marché qui alimentent les recommandations stratégiques. Vous traduirez la recherche et les données de performance en implications claires qui orientent la prise de décision dans toutes les équipes.
 Stratégie de canaux et planification des investissements: Vous mettrez à profit votre expertise approfondie en stratégie et en planification média pour définir le mix de canaux, le séquençage et la logique d'investissement qui soutiennent les objectifs de croissance. Vous alimenterez des plans média full-funnel qui font évoluer les programmes média des clients au-delà du marketing de performance et couvrent chaque étape du parcours client, de la notoriété à la fidélisation. Vous collaborerez avec les leaders média, CRM, SEO et expérience numérique pour que les choix de canaux et l'allocation budgétaire soient alignés sur le cadre stratégique global.
 Cadres de mesure et interprétation de la performance: Vous établirez des cadres de mesure qui définissent le succès avant l'activation. Vous aiderez les équipes à interpréter les signaux de performance, pour que les insights guident les décisions plutôt que de simplement alimenter les rapports.
 Récit stratégique de la performance: Vous dirigerez le récit stratégique des revues d'affaires trimestrielles (QBR) et des discussions de planification, en expliquant ce qui s'est passé, pourquoi, ce que nous avons appris et quelles actions doivent suivre. Votre récit reliera les données, les insights et les implications d'affaires pour en tirer des recommandations claires.
 Partenariat stratégique avec les clients: Vous serez un partenaire stratégique pour les parties prenantes clients et mènerez avec assurance les conversations sur les occasions de croissance, les priorités de planification et les recommandations stratégiques. Vous amènerez les discussions au-delà de l'exécution tactique, vers un impact d'affaires à long terme.
 Alignement stratégique multidisciplinaire: Vous ferez le lien entre les équipes média, création, SEO, CRM, web et analytique pour que la stratégie soit intégrée de façon constante à l'exécution. Vous harmoniserez les indicateurs clés, les messages, les stratégies de canaux et les cadres de mesure afin d'assurer une intention d'affaires claire.
 Habilitation stratégique des équipes: Vous outillerez les équipes de comptes et de livraison avec des cadres et des conseils qui rehaussent la qualité et la cohérence de la réflexion stratégique dans toute l'agence. Votre travail aidera à simplifier la planification et à clarifier les défis complexes.
 Normes et cadres stratégiques: Vous contribuerez à l'évolution des cadres, des guides et des outils de planification stratégique de l'agence. Vous aiderez à intégrer la stratégie aux briefs, aux cycles de planification et aux rythmes d'optimisation, pour qu'elle devienne une discipline centrale de nos opérations.
 Leadership éclairé et soutien aux nouvelles affaires: Vous contribuerez aux points de vue de l'agence, aux guides sectoriels et aux récits de croissance qui renforcent notre différenciation sur le marché. Vous appuierez le développement des affaires par un récit stratégique et un positionnement fondé sur les insights.
 Des déplacements occasionnels pourraient être requis pour des événements d’entreprise et des conférences de l’industrie. 
 Compétences et qualifications:
 Solide expérience dans l'élaboration de stratégies marketing intégrées couvrant plusieurs canaux et disciplines.
 Expérience démontrée en stratégie et planification média, avec la capacité de concevoir des plans média full-funnel à plusieurs étapes qui amènent les programmes des clients au-delà du marketing de performance, vers des stratégies de marque et de demande en haut et au milieu de l'entonnoir.
 Capacité à traduire des objectifs d'affaires en une orientation stratégique claire qui guide les équipes multidisciplinaires.
 Solides compétences analytiques et capacité à tirer des insights pertinents des données de performance, de la recherche et de la veille de marché.
 Pensée systémique et capacité à comprendre comment les messages, les canaux, l'expérience client et la mesure s'articulent.
 Excellentes aptitudes en narration et en communication, avec la capacité de présenter des idées complexes de façon claire et convaincante.
 Solides compétences en animation et en collaboration, avec la capacité de rallier des équipes multidisciplinaires autour de priorités stratégiques communes.
 Prestance et assurance lors de la présentation de recommandations stratégiques à des parties prenantes clients de haut niveau.
 Esprit de croissance, ouverture à la rétroaction et souci d'amélioration continue.
 Solides compétences organisationnelles et capacité à gérer simultanément plusieurs cycles de planification et initiatives stratégiques.
 Aisance dans des contextes ambigus et capacité à apporter de la clarté à des défis d'affaires complexe
 Formation et expérience:
 Plus de 5 ans d'expérience en stratégie marketing, stratégie intégrée, stratégie de marque, stratégie et planification média ou stratégie de croissance, en agence ou chez l'annonceur.
 Expérience démontrée dans l'élaboration et l'évolution de stratégies média couvrant l'ensemble du parcours client, sans se limiter aux canaux de performance en bas de l'entonnoir.
 Expérience démontrée dans l'élaboration de stratégies marketing intégrées et multicanales.
 Expérience dans la conduite de la planification annuelle, de l'élaboration de feuilles de route stratégiques et des discussions de croissance avec les clients.
 Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes média, création, expérience numérique, CRM et analytique.
 Baccalauréat en marketing, en administration des affaires, en communication ou dans un domaine connexe.
 Une expérience dans le secteur CPG ou B2B est un atout, mais n'est pas requise.
 Une expérience dans le secteur de l'éducation (établissements à but lucratif ou sans but lucratif) est fortement souhaitée.
 Attentes liées à l’IA
 Chez Level, la maîtrise des outils d'IA est un élément central de votre rôle, pas un simple atout. Votre succès dans ce poste repose non seulement sur votre expertise, mais aussi sur votre capacité à intégrer activement l'IA dans votre façon de travailler.
 Vous devrez:
 Expérimenter continuellement avec des outils d'IA (p. ex. ChatGPT, Midjourney, Claude, Perplexity) pour améliorer la rapidité, la qualité et l'impact de votre travail (p. ex. rédiger des briefs, résumer de la recherche, analyser des tendances, générer des cadres stratégiques préliminaires, repérer des modèles dans de grands ensembles de données).
 Documenter et partager de façon proactive ce que vous apprenez, comme vos requêtes, vos améliorations de processus et vos cas d'utilisation, pour que les autres en profitent et que nous progressions ensemble.
 Aborder l'IA avec un esprit itératif en raffinant au fil du temps la façon dont vous l'appliquez à votre travail. La première idée est rarement la meilleure: tester, ajuster et améliorer fait partie du processus.
 Accepter l'inconfort, surtout lorsque des outils ou des façons de faire vous semblent peu familiers. C'est en sortant de sa zone de confort et de sa routine qu'on grandit.
 L'IA n'est pas un raccourci, c'est une compétence. Vous devrez l'utiliser comme multiplicateur de force pour la création, la stratégie et l'exécution, et non comme substitut à un travail réfléchi. À mesure que nos outils évoluent, votre capacité à vous adapter et à mener le changement jouera un rôle clé dans votre performance et votre croissance chez Level.
 Nos valeurs fondamentales
 No Ego, All In 
Ici, on ne dit pas « ce n’est pas mon travail ». Nous gagnons ensemble, nous mettons la main à la pâte quand c’est nécessaire et nous nous soucions davantage du résultat que de l’organigramme.
 Better Every Day 
Nous voulons recevoir la rétroaction — même quand elle pique. Nous testons, apprenons, nous adaptons et continuons à élever la barre.
 Relentless for Results 
L’activité ne vaut rien sans résultats. Nous nous concentrons sur le travail qui fait avancer l’entreprise.
 Driven by Truth 
Nous remettons les hypothèses en question, suivons les données et disons aux clients ce qu’ils doivent entendre — pas seulement ce qui est facile à dire.
 Avantages et bénéfices
 Chez Level, nous soutenons nos équipes aux États-Unis et au Canada avec des avantages conçus pour favoriser la flexibilité, le bien-être et la croissance à long terme.
 Télétravail complet aux États-Unis et au Canada, allocation mensuelle pour le travail à domicile et vendredis d’été
 Congés généreux, incluant des congés payés illimités aux États-Unis, des vacances concurrentielles au Canada et des options de congé parental/familial
 Avantages complets en santé, soutien en santé mentale et assurances invalidité et vie payées par l’entreprise
 Cotisations de retraite de l’employeur, 401(k) aux États-Unis et contribution REER au Canada
 Évaluations de performance trimestrielles et occasions d’avancement professionnel
 Priorité au télétravail
 Ce rôle est ouvert aux résidentes et résidents des États-Unis et du Canada et se fait entièrement à distance. Des déplacements occasionnels pourraient être requis pour des événements d’entreprise et des conférences de l’industrie. Nous ne sommes pas en mesure de commanditer des visas pour le moment.
 Level est fondée sur l’inclusion
 Nous sommes engagés envers la diversité, l’équité, l’inclusion et le sentiment d’appartenance. Level est fière d’être un employeur souscrivant au principe de l’égalité d’accès à l’emploi — nous célébrons ce qui fait de vous la personne que vous êtes. Level Agency offre des mesures d'adaptation raisonnables aux personnes candidates en situation de handicap tout au long du processus de recrutement. Si vous avez besoin d'une mesure d'adaptation, veuillez nous en informer lors de votre candidature ou de votre processus d'entrevue.
 Prêt(e) à postuler?
 Cliquez ci-dessous pour soumettre votre CV. Vous répondrez aussi à quelques questions réfléchies, alors prenez le temps de bien le faire.
 Ce qui nous importe le plus, c’est votre façon de penser, de bâtir et de créer de l’impact — pas que votre parcours ait été parfaitement linéaire.
 Bâtissons quelque chose ensemble. 
 Divulgation sur l'utilisation de l'IA dans l'embauche 
 Nous utilisons des outils assistés par l'IA pour appuyer certaines étapes de notre processus d'embauche, notamment la présélection des CV ainsi que la prise de notes ou la production de résumés d'entrevues. Ces outils soutiennent le jugement humain, mais ne le remplacent pas. Toutes les décisions d'embauche sont prises par l'équipe d'embauche de Level.

jobs.title: Senior Director - Enterprise Performance, Evaluation and Strategic Initiatives
jobs.description:
Position Title: Senior Director – Enterprise Performance, Evaluation and Strategic Initiatives
 Employment Status: Permanent Full Time 
 Position Status: This is a Non-Bargaining Unit position
 This posting is for a new vacancy.
 Hours of Work: Monday to Friday, 35 Hours
 Position Reports to: Chief Executive Officer
 Salary Range: $ 125,000 - $140,000, commensurate on skills and experience, plus participation in HOOPP and Group Benefits.
 Primary work location: Oshawa (Hybrid work environment); Staff may be requested to work out of other DCHC’s sites in Pickering, Whitby, Ajax, Oshawa South and Oshawa North (Airport Road) as required.
 Direct Reports: 5 
 ·        Manager 
 ·        Quality Improvement Coordinator - 1
 ·        Health Information Specialist - 1
 ·        Data Analyst - 2

Organization 
 Who We Are: Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is a charitable registered organization that provides integrated, accessible, and equitable community-based primary care, wellness services, and health education for Durham community members facing barriers to health and well-being.

 Who We Serve: DCHC offers equity-focused programs and services for priority populations, including Indigenous peoples, Black communities, 2SLGBTQI+ community members, newcomers to Canada, seniors, and clients without a family doctor. This approach helps community members access both preventive care and care when they are ill.

 How We Work: Our interprofessional team includes physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, counsellors, dietitians, outreach workers, medical secretaries, and administrative staff. Together, we place each client at the centre of care and respond to their needs through integrated clinical care, wellness support, and health education.

 Why Join Now: This is an exciting time to join DCHC as we advance an energizing path toward greater impact in local health care. Guided by our Strategic Plan, Theory of Change, brand, client stories, and resources, we are diversifying, expanding, and strengthening how we serve the community.

 Position Overview 
 Durham Community Health Center (DCHC) is seeking an exceptional, self-driven leader to take on the role of Senior Director, Enterprise Performance, Evaluation and Strategic Initiatives. The role demands a leader who thrives in complexity, excels in driving enterprise-wide performance, and is relentless in the pursuit of excellence.

 At DCHC we are committed to a collaborative culture where strategic thinking, execution discipline and shared leadership are at the core of everything we do. As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the Senior Director will be responsible for aligning enterprise performance, strategic initiatives, and quality improvement with DCHC’s long-term vision.

 This role is a unique opportunity for an innovative leader to build high-impact frameworks for evaluation, decision support, special project execution and quality transformation. The right candidate will be a visionary, a doer and a collaborator; someone who can seamlessly transition between strategy and execution while fostering an organizational culture of continuous improvement and strategic excellence.

 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 
 As a member of the Executive Leadership Team and strategic advisor to the CEO, the Senior Director provides enterprise leadership across strategy execution, performance intelligence, transformation, risk, quality, accreditation, and organizational alignment.

 1. Enterprise Strategy & Execution 
 ·         Translate DCHC’s strategic plan into clear annual priorities, business operating plans, performance measures, and funder accountabilities.
 ·         Lead enterprise strategy execution and monitor progress against strategic commitments, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and long-term strategic objectives.
 ·         Ensure alignment between Board priorities, CEO direction, ELT accountabilities, resource management, and organizational initiatives execution.

 2. Enterprise Performance & Intelligence 
 ·         Establish DCHC’s enterprise performance management framework.
 ·         Develop integrated, real-time dashboards, scorecards, quality indicators, and performance reporting tools.
 ·         Lead enterprise analytics, program evaluation, KPIs, outcome measurement, governance reporting, and data-informed decision-making.
 ·         Provide the CEO and ELT with timely intelligence focusing on trends to support strategic decisions and performance improvement.

 3. Strategic Initiatives & Transformation 
 ·         Lead CEO and ELT-sponsored strategic initiatives, complex enterprise projects, and transformational initiatives that improve service delivery and operational effectiveness.
 ·         Establish clear governance framework, milestones, accountabilities, and measures for all organizational initiatives aligned to DCHC corporate balance scorecard.

 4. Enterprise Risk, Quality & Organizational Excellence 
 ·         Lead the enterprise risk management strategy, including proactive risk identification, mitigation, monitoring, annual planning, and reporting.
 ·         Lead DCHC’s enterprise Quality Improvement and accreditation strategy, including organization-wide QI frameworks, and compliance reporting.
 ·         Integrate quality, risk, performance, evaluation, and continuous improvement into one enterprise framework.
 ·         Strengthen organizational resilience, accountability, and readiness for emerging challenges.

 5. CEO Advisory & Enterprise Alignment 
 ·         Serve as a strategic advisor to the Office of the CEO.
 ·         Provide executive analysis, strategic options, decision support, and recommendations that enhance program and organizational effectiveness.
 ·         Lead CEO Office strategic operating plans and priority tracking.
 ·         Identify and resolve cross-portfolio dependencies, competing priorities, and organizational barriers that could impede enterprise execution.
 ·         Champion One DCHC, One Strategy, One Enterprise.

 Strategic Mandate 
 The Senior Director ensures DCHC has the clarity, intelligence, discipline, and execution capability to turn strategy into measurable organizational and community collective impact.

 QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE 
 Education & Certifications 
 ·        Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, Business Administration, or a related field (master’s preferred) 
 ·        PMP, Lean Six Sigma, Change Management or a relevant performance excellence certification is an asset.

 Experience & Skills 
 •        7-10 years of progressive senior leadership experience in enterprise performance, strategic execution, quality improvement, program evaluation, risk management, or transformation leadership.   
 •        Proven success in leading high-impact initiatives, enterprise-wide projects, and complex change management efforts.  
 •        Strong ability to analyze data, identify trends, and translate insights into strategic action.
 •        Deep understanding of Ontario’s healthcare transformation, integrated care models, and emerging policy trends.  
 •        Exceptional leadership, stakeholder engagement, and executive communication skills.  
 •        Demonstrated ability to lead in a collaborative, fast-moving, and high-accountability environment.
 What Sets This Role Apart?  
 •        This is a high-stakes, high-impact leadership role. It requires:  
 o   A strategic powerhouse who can execute with precision.  
 o   A collaborative leader who thrives in a multi-disciplinary, fast-paced environment.  
 o   A change agent who is comfortable leading transformational initiatives and navigating complexity.  
 o   A data-driven decision-maker who can synthesize insights into actionable strategies.  
 Why Join DCHC? 
 •        Impact at Scale – Drive transformational change in a high-performing primary care organization.  
 •        Enterprise-Level Innovation – Lead quality, performance, and strategic initiatives at the highest level.  
 •        Leadership Growth – Competitive compensation, HOOPP pension, and ongoing professional development.  
 Benefits 
 ·        Comprehensive health benefits
 ·        Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP)
 ·        Growth and Development opportunities; annual professional development allowance 

 Full vaccination against COVID-19 is mandatory for this position (DCHC will however adhere to its duty to accommodate those who are unable to be fully vaccinated for a reason related to a human right protected ground). 
 DCHC encourages applications from individuals who reflect the diversity of the communities served, including Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, and other equity-deserving groups. 
 Application Process: 
 1.        While we thank all applicants for their interest in applying, only those qualified and considered for an interview will be contacted. All applicant submissions will be kept on file for six months, for future consideration.
 2.        All applicants are encouraged to provide a valid email address for communication purposes. Applicants may receive written correspondence regarding this job posting directly to the email address provided on their resume. As an applicant, it is your responsibility to ensure that you check your email regularly.
 3.        All positions are subject to the successful completion of the following pre-employment conditions for all external hires: Reference Checks; and Criminal Background checks (including Vulnerable Sector Screening).
 4.        Please be advised that AI Technology supports the screening process of applications. All final hiring decisions are made by our recruitment team.
 Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is committed to creating an inclusive environment that welcomes and celebrates diversity so that all employees have the opportunity to thrive.  DCHC will comply with all applicable standards as set out in the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 (AODA), the provisions of the Ontario Human Rights Code, and any other applicable legislation.  Accessibility: If you have accessibility needs and require alternate formats or other accommodation, please contact our Talent and Culture team at 905-723-0036, or by email  to recruiting@durhamchc.ca

 Position Overview 
 Durham Community Health Center (DCHC) is seeking an exceptional, self-driven leader to take on the role of Senior Director, Enterprise Performance, Evaluation and Strategic Initiatives. The role demands a leader who thrives in complexity, excels in driving enterprise-wide performance, and is relentless in the pursuit of excellence.

 At DCHC we are committed to a collaborative culture where strategic thinking, execution discipline and shared leadership are at the core of everything we do. As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the Senior Director will be responsible for aligning enterprise performance, strategic initiatives, and quality improvement with DCHC’s long-term vision.

jobs.title: Finance Executive Director
jobs.description:
Ready to lead the financial future of a brand with heart and purpose?
 At Hadley Designs, we believe every product should fill homes with beauty, learning, and inspiration. We design screen-free learning tools that help children fall in love with learning and help parents feel proud of how they nurture that growth.
 As our Finance Executive Director, you’ll be the architect of scalable systems that fuel that mission. You’ll bring precision, foresight, and strategic clarity to every financial decision, guiding the company’s growth toward $100M and beyond with confidence and discipline.
 You won’t just manage numbers. You’ll empower a purpose-driven team to think bigger, move faster, and build a lasting legacy.

 About Hadley Designs
 Hadley Designs is a family-founded brand redefining early education through creativity, beauty, and connection. We design screen-free learning tools that spark curiosity and confidence in children while giving parents peace of mind.
 We believe learning should be fun and engaging. Beautiful design creates better learning. We don’t just sell products. We shape futures.

 About the Role
 Your Core Focus
 You’ll own the full finance function, building scalable systems, managing cash flow, driving profitability, and leading financial strategy to support Hadley Designs’ next era of growth.

 What You’ll Do
 Deliver accurate, audit-ready financials by the 20th of each month with full account reconciliation and zero material errors
 Build and maintain a 12-month rolling cash forecast, updated weekly, ensuring perfect liquidity and visibility
 Lead the annual budgeting and forecasting process across all departments with ≤10% variance between forecast and actual results
 Develop automated systems and workflows that reduce manual reporting time by at least 25% within your first year
 Partner with leadership to implement initiatives that increase profitability and improve EBITDA by 2 percentage points in your first 12 months
 Create and document SOPs for close, forecasting, cash flow, and reporting processes
 Implement new systems for expense management, travel, and purchasing by Month 6
 Produce insightful financial dashboards and KPIs that drive better decision-making
 Partner cross-functionally with Product, Sales, and Operations to align growth, cash flow, and inventory planning
 Evaluate technology solutions (ERP, reporting tools) that prepare the company for scale

 How Success Is Measured
 100% of monthly financials delivered on time and error-free
 0 overdrafts, late fees, or missed payments
 ≤10% variance between forecasted and actual EBITDA
 12-month rolling cash forecast maintained weekly
 SOPs for all finance processes documented within 3 months
 System improvements reducing manual work by 25% in Year 1
 Trailing-12-month EBITDA margin up 2 points within first year

 Who You Are 
 You’re a strategic, detail-oriented leader who thrives on clarity, accuracy, and impact. You know how to scale systems, guide teams through growth, and communicate financial insight in plain English. You’re not just reporting numbers, you’re building the foundation for smart, sustainable expansion.

jobs.title: Head of Data & AI
jobs.description:
About Burq 
 Burq started with an ambitious mission: to turn the complex process of offering delivery into a simple, turnkey solution. It’s a big mission, and now we want you to join us in making it even bigger. 🚀
 We’re proud to be recognized as one of Fast Company’s Best Workplaces for Innovators and a 2025 Inc. Magazine Power Partner, awards that highlight how we’re redefining the future of logistics while empowering our partners to grow.
 Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors like Village Global, the fund whose investors include Bill Gates, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, Reid Hoffman, and Sara Blakely, we’ve built a world-class team across the globe.
 We operate at scale but remain small enough for every person to have a massive impact. There’s a lot of important work ahead, and joining Burq means the opportunity to grow faster than ever while doing the most meaningful work of your career.

 Here’s a quick overview of what you will be doing:

 The Role
 We're looking for a Head of Data & AI to build the intelligence that powers Burq. 
 You'll build a world-class data-and-ML platform: the systems that turn data into models which make every delivery decision smarter and agents that automate the work the industry still does by hand. You'll set the strategy, make the hard architecture and modeling calls, ship models into production that move the business, and build the team to do it at scale.
 This is a player-coach role. You'll lead and grow the data and ML team while staying deeply hands-on — making architecture calls, reviewing engineering and modeling work, and ensuring the platform serves both product and business goals. You'll partner closely with the Head of Engineering, and with product and AI leadership on how intelligence shows up in the product.

 What You'll Do
 Data Platform

 Own the full data platform — the warehouse, streaming and batch ingestion, the semantic layer, and BI infrastructure.
 Define and enforce data governance — access management, quality standards, and a well-modeled, trustworthy "gold" layer.
 Make the warehouse the source of truth for operational, product, and financial analytics.

 Intelligence & Machine Learning 

 Build the models that power delivery intelligence — forecasting, prediction, optimization, matching/allocation, and reliability scoring that turn our data into better real-time decisions.
 Stand up the ML systems that make this real and reliable: feature pipelines, training, serving, evaluation, and drift monitoring.
 Design the learning loop — instrument decisions and outcomes so models continuously improve.
 Drive the AI agent initiative to production, partnering with product and engineering on the surrounding workflows.

 Team & Stakeholders

 Manage and grow the data and ML team (starting from a small core) — hire data engineers, analytics engineers, and data scientists/ML engineers as the platform matures.
 Establish a clear intake process for ad hoc data requests so the team works from a roadmap, not in reactive mode.
 Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Finance on data-driven analyses and decisions.

We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients. 

 At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute. 

 To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com 

 What you'll be doing 

 The People, Culture and Talent team helps shape the experiences that support our people, our culture and our workplace so we can help make our clients’ ambitions a reality.  As Director, Inclusion - Data, Insights and Operations, you’ll lead the data, reporting, financial management and business operations activities that support the execution of CIBC’s enterprise Inclusion strategy. You’ll build and manage analytics, dashboards, scorecards and performance measures that help leaders understand progress, identify opportunities and make informed decisions. You’ll partner across Human Resources and business teams to translate workforce and portfolio data into clear, actionable insights and reporting. You’ll also oversee budget planning and financial management for the Inclusion portfolio, strengthen reporting routines and controls, and drive continuous improvement. In this leadership role, you’ll help create a more integrated, measurable and effective approach to advancing inclusion across the enterprise.

 At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote. 

 How you'll succeed 

 Lead analytics and reportin g - Develop, implement and manage Inclusion analytics, dashboards, scorecards and key performance indicators that measure progress against enterprise priorities and commitments.
 Generate actionable insights - Translate workforce, demographic and portfolio data into clear trends, risks and opportunities, and provide recommendations that support decision-making and continuous improvement.

 Who you are

new_jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do. 

 At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

 When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

 Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

 Job Description: 
 About the Role 

 The Corporate AVP, Underwriting Risk & Governance is accountable for maintaining the organization's underwriting philosophy, risk appetite, technical standards, and governance framework across all life and health insurance businesses. The role serves as a corporate risk subject matter expert on mortality, morbidity, product, underwriting, and fraud risks, providing underwriting risk management guidance to business units globally, with particular emphasis on emerging risks, high-net-worth markets, and the impact of underwriting and product design decisions on long-term business performance.

 The incumbent will lead the evaluation and approval of underwriting and product-related risk initiatives, assess the mortality and morbidity implications of underwriting requirement changes, product innovations, and distribution strategies, and ensure alignment with corporate risk management objectives, with primary focus on our Asia business units and Private Wealth business. The role provides technical leadership to underwriters and input to actuarial, product development, and risk management teams on underwriting-specific risk while championing sound underwriting practices, risk governance, and sustainable growth.

 Operating in a highly collaborative, consultative, and project-oriented environment, the Corporate AVP, Underwriting Risk & Governance will lead complex initiatives across the Asia business units and jurisdictions, influence business unit underwriting leadership and risk management decision-making, and represent the organization on underwriting and insurance industry matters under the direction of the Corporate Chief Underwriter.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Enterprise Underwriting Governance 
 Support and champion corporate underwriting philosophy, risk appetite, and underwriting governance standards.

 Provide enterprise oversight of underwriting practices across life, health, critical illness, disability, and medical reimbursement products.

 Evaluate proposed changes to underwriting requirements, underwriting evidence, accelerated underwriting programs, automation initiatives, and digital underwriting solutions.

 Assess and communicate the mortality and morbidity implications associated with underwriting and product design changes.

 Mortality and Morbidity Risk Management 
 Evaluate mortality and morbidity risks associated with existing and proposed products, underwriting methodologies, and distribution strategies.

 Assess the impact of product features, underwriting evidence requirements, and benefit structures on expected mortality and morbidity outcomes.

 Partner with actuarial, product, and risk management teams to monitor emerging experience trends and recommend mitigation strategies.

 Provide technical leadership on mortality and morbidity risk management across multiple markets.

 Product and Anti-Selection Risk Assessment 
 Assess product design features for anti-selection, fraud, claims, and sustainability risks.

 Identify underwriting controls, medical requirements, and risk management measures necessary to mitigate adverse selection and fraud exposure.

 Provide risk guidance during new product development and product enhancement activities.

 Evaluate the potential impact of product design changes on underwriting outcomes and claims experience.

 Fraud Risk Oversight 
 Identify emerging fraud risks and vulnerabilities within underwriting and product frameworks.

 Recommend underwriting, medical, and operational controls designed to mitigate fraud exposure.

 Partner with claims, investigations, and risk management teams to identify trends and strengthen preventive measures.

 High - Net - Worth and Complex Risk Expertise 
 Provide technical leadership on high-net-worth and Private Wealth underwriting practices, particularly within Asian markets.

 Evaluate large face amount and complex financial underwriting cases.

 Monitor market developments and emerging risk trends impacting high-net-worth and Private Wealth business.

 Support business units in developing prudent underwriting strategies for complex and high-exposure risks.

 Retention and Reinsurance Management 
 Provide leadership and guidance regarding retention management practices.

 Evaluate retention limits, concentration risk, and reinsurance effectiveness.

 Partner with reinsurance stakeholders as permitted to ensure alignment between underwriting strategies and risk transfer objectives.

 Strategic Leadership 
 Lead complex cross-functional underwriting initiatives involving multiple business units, jurisdictions, and product lines.

 Influence senior leaders and business partners on underwriting, mortality, morbidity, and product risk matters.

 Provide strategic recommendations balancing growth opportunities with responsible risk management.

 Serve as a trusted advisor to the Corporate Chief Underwriter on emerging underwriting and insurance risks.

 Technical Thought Leadership 
 Research emerging medical, underwriting, product, and industry developments.

 Participate in the development and maintenance of underwriting manuals, medical guidelines, and risk assessment standards.

 Translate emerging medical evidence and industry research into practical underwriting guidance.

 Represent the organization externally through industry associations, conferences, forums, and professional organizations.

 What you'll need to succeed 
 Minimum 15 years of progressive life and health underwriting experience.

 Minimum 5 years holding an individual underwriting approval authority of at least $30 million (preferred).

 Significant experience assessing complex mortality and morbidity risks.

 Experience underwriting high-net-worth and large face amount business, including exposure to Asian insurance markets.

 Demonstrated experience evaluating underwriting implications of life, health, disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, and medical reimbursement products.

 Proven experience leading complex underwriting, governance, or risk initiatives across multiple business units or jurisdictions.

 Experience working with reinsurance and retention management frameworks.

 Experience developing underwriting philosophy, guidelines, manuals, and risk governance standards.

 Proven ability to influence business risk management and underwriting leaders.

 Strong strategic thinking and risk assessment capabilities.

 Exceptional communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.

 Ability to work independently with minimal direction while managing multiple concurrent priorities.

 Strong collaboration skills with the ability to drive alignment across diverse stakeholders.

 Comfortable operating in a dynamic environment focused on governance, consultation, project leadership, innovation, and enterprise risk oversight rather than production underwriting activities.

 Preferred Designations 
 FALU

 FLMI

 Additional designations in risk management, supplemental health, or related disciplines.

 What's in it for you 
 Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.

 In 2024, Sun Life ranked among the top 100 most sustainable global corporations by Corporate Knights for the 15th consecutive year, leading Canadian insurers. 

 We are proud to be on the 2024 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work. 

 We’re also listed as one of the Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams.

 Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.

 Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to support your well-being.

 The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results. 

 Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

 Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

 We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

 We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling. 

 We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

 Salary Range: 
155,000/155 000 - 225,000/225 000

Underwriting - Individual

new_jobs.title: Finance Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
Ready to lead the financial future of a brand with heart and purpose?
 At Hadley Designs, we believe every product should fill homes with beauty, learning, and inspiration. We design screen-free learning tools that help children fall in love with learning and help parents feel proud of how they nurture that growth.
 As our Finance Executive Director, you’ll be the architect of scalable systems that fuel that mission. You’ll bring precision, foresight, and strategic clarity to every financial decision, guiding the company’s growth toward $100M and beyond with confidence and discipline.
 You won’t just manage numbers. You’ll empower a purpose-driven team to think bigger, move faster, and build a lasting legacy.

 About Hadley Designs
 Hadley Designs is a family-founded brand redefining early education through creativity, beauty, and connection. We design screen-free learning tools that spark curiosity and confidence in children while giving parents peace of mind.
 We believe learning should be fun and engaging. Beautiful design creates better learning. We don’t just sell products. We shape futures.

 About the Role
 Your Core Focus
 You’ll own the full finance function, building scalable systems, managing cash flow, driving profitability, and leading financial strategy to support Hadley Designs’ next era of growth.

 What You’ll Do
 Deliver accurate, audit-ready financials by the 20th of each month with full account reconciliation and zero material errors
 Build and maintain a 12-month rolling cash forecast, updated weekly, ensuring perfect liquidity and visibility
 Lead the annual budgeting and forecasting process across all departments with ≤10% variance between forecast and actual results
 Develop automated systems and workflows that reduce manual reporting time by at least 25% within your first year
 Partner with leadership to implement initiatives that increase profitability and improve EBITDA by 2 percentage points in your first 12 months
 Create and document SOPs for close, forecasting, cash flow, and reporting processes
 Implement new systems for expense management, travel, and purchasing by Month 6
 Produce insightful financial dashboards and KPIs that drive better decision-making
 Partner cross-functionally with Product, Sales, and Operations to align growth, cash flow, and inventory planning
 Evaluate technology solutions (ERP, reporting tools) that prepare the company for scale

 How Success Is Measured
 100% of monthly financials delivered on time and error-free
 0 overdrafts, late fees, or missed payments
 ≤10% variance between forecasted and actual EBITDA
 12-month rolling cash forecast maintained weekly
 SOPs for all finance processes documented within 3 months
 System improvements reducing manual work by 25% in Year 1
 Trailing-12-month EBITDA margin up 2 points within first year

 Who You Are 
 You’re a strategic, detail-oriented leader who thrives on clarity, accuracy, and impact. You know how to scale systems, guide teams through growth, and communicate financial insight in plain English. You’re not just reporting numbers, you’re building the foundation for smart, sustainable expansion.
